label: National Palace (Palacio Nacional)
sub: Presidential residence and seat of executive power; site of Sheinbaum's daily press conferences (mañaneras). Location of constitutional oath-taking ceremony on October 1, 2024.

label: Chamber of Deputies (San Lázaro)
sub: Where Morena's supermajority coalition passed the judicial reform, autonomous agency dissolution, social program constitutionalization, and energy nationalization amendments throughout late 2024.

label: Senate of the Republic
sub: Site of the November 28, 2024 vote dissolving INAI, COFECE, and five other autonomous constitutional agencies. Senate protesters broke into the building during judicial reform debates in September 2024.

label: Supreme Court (SCJN)
sub: Reconfigured September 1, 2025 with 9 justices (reduced from 11), all elected in the June 2025 judicial elections and perceived as Morena-aligned. Hugo Aguilar Ortiz serves as new Chief Justice.

label: National Electoral Institute (INE)
sub: Oversaw the historic June 2025 judicial elections for 2,681 judicial posts. Absorbed some transparency oversight functions after INAI's dissolution in late 2024.

label: Secretariat of Security (SSPC)
sub: Federal security and intelligence coordination headquarters under Secretary Omar García Harfuch. December 2024 reform made SSPC coordinating body of the National Intelligence System with expanded criminal investigation powers. May 21, 2026: site of bilateral security talks with incoming U.S. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin (confirmed March 2026, replacing Kristi Noem) — Mullin's first official visit to Mexico.

label: U.S. Embassy, Mexico City
sub: Located on Paseo de la Reforma. Normal diplomatic protocols with Ambassador Ken Salazar resumed on October 2, 2024 after AMLO-era suspension. Site of major bilateral coordination meetings on tariffs, deportations, and security.

label: San Ysidro – Tijuana POE
sub: World's busiest land port of entry. Primary processing point for Mexico's mass deportation reception program (México te Abraza). 10,000 National Guard troops deployed nearby in Feb 2025 to pause tariff threats.

label: Nogales Border Crossing
sub: Key US-Mexico port of entry in Sonora/Arizona corridor. Active National Guard deployment zone as part of Sheinbaum's February 2025 border security surge. On March 27, 2026, a small group of U.S. military personnel briefly crossed into Mexican territory here; Sheinbaum called it an unintentional incident reversed immediately, ruling out a sovereignty violation.

label: Ciudad Juárez – El Paso POE
sub: Major crossing point for both migration and commercial trade. One of nine border reception centers established by Mexico under the México te Abraza deportee repatriation program.

label: Nuevo Laredo – Laredo POE
sub: Single largest commercial cargo crossing in the entire US-Mexico border, processing over $300 billion in annual trade. Key pressure point during 25% tariff threat in early 2025; USMCA-compliant goods remained exempt.

label: Matamoros – Brownsville (Rio Grande Water Dispute Zone)
sub: Located in the Rio Grande Valley agricultural zone at the center of the 1944 water treaty dispute. Texas cited $994M in crop losses from Mexico's shortfall. A 5% tariff was imposed December 9, 2025 and lifted after December 12 agreement.

label: Monterrey — Premier Nearshoring Hub
sub: Mexico's industrial capital and leading nearshoring destination. Home to the Hofusan Industrial Park (40+ Chinese companies) and clusters in automotive, logistics, and ICT. Anchor of the Nuevo León industrial corridor targeted by Plan México's 15 special economic zones.

label: Querétaro — Aerospace and Advanced Manufacturing Hub
sub: Major aerospace and advanced manufacturing cluster in the Bajío region. Significant nearshoring expansion during 2024–2025; part of the industrial corridor targeted by Plan México to reduce Chinese import dependence.

label: Guadalajara — 'Silicon Valley of Mexico'
sub: Mexico's ICT and tech services hub. Also the base of operations for CJNG, which is headquartered in Jalisco state. The CJNG Teuchitlán training camp was discovered 50km west of the city in March 2025.

label: Teuchitlán, Jalisco — CJNG Rancho Izaguirre Camp
sub: Discovered March 5, 2025 by missing persons volunteers: ~200 pairs of shoes, 3 makeshift crematoriums, charred remains, and military training infrastructure. Mayor José Murguía Santiago arrested May 3, 2025 on organized crime and forced disappearance charges.

label: Culiacán, Sinaloa — Cartel Civil War Ground Zero
sub: Capital of Sinaloa state and ground zero of the Chapitos vs. Mayiza faction civil war that erupted after El Mayo Zambada's July 2024 U.S. arrest. Over 2,197 homicides since the conflict began; state homicide rate up approximately 400%.

label: Chilpancingo, Guerrero — High Violence Capital
sub: State capital of Guerrero, one of Mexico's most violent states. Security analysts describe parts of the region as 'near-ungovernable' due to cartel territorial control. Key data point for debates about the 'hugs not bullets' security policy.

label: Saltillo, Coahuila — Automotive Production Hub
sub: Home to major GM and Chrysler/Stellantis production facilities. Key beneficiary of USMCA auto content rules and nearshoring investment surge during 2024–2025. Part of the northern industrial corridor targeted by Plan México.

label: Tijuana — Electronics & Medical Devices Manufacturing
sub: Major hub for electronics, medical devices, and aerospace manufacturing due to US proximity. Dual function as a commerce zone and deportee reception center under México te Abraza. Part of Plan México's special economic zone framework.

label: Aguascalientes — Nissan & Auto Parts Hub
sub: Home to Nissan's major Mexican production facility and a dense network of auto parts suppliers. Benefiting from USMCA rules of origin requirements driving nearshoring investment. Included in Plan México's industrial zone initiative.

label: Guanajuato — Industrial Hub Under Security Pressure
sub: Mexico's most homicide-affected state in absolute numbers (2,539 in 2025). Home to major automotive and agricultural industries targeted by Plan México nearshoring policy. The CJNG-CSRL conflict has persisted despite federal security operations.

label: Chiapas — Southern Border Migration Zone
sub: Key entry point for Central American migration into Mexico, with proximity to Guatemala. National Guard deployments to Chiapas were part of Mexico's February 2025 border surge to prevent migrants from reaching the US-Mexico border. Major processing zone under México te Abraza.

label: Dos Bocas Refinery (Tabasco)
sub: Pemex's flagship new refinery — the crown jewel of AMLO's energy sovereignty agenda. On March 24, 2026, an explosion triggered an oil spill, prompting a federal emergency response and FGR investigation. Environmental groups raised concerns about marine ecosystem damage. The incident reignited debate over the $17-billion public investment and Pemex's operational safety record.

label: Estadio Banorte (formerly Azteca) — World Cup 2026 Venue
sub: Reopened March 28, 2026 after ~2 years of World Cup renovation works. Mexico drew Portugal 0-0 in the inaugural friendly match. The renamed stadium is one of three Mexican FIFA 2026 venues alongside Guadalajara's Estadio Akron and Monterrey's Estadio BBVA. Protesters gathered outside over Mexico's 130,000+ missing persons and stadium renovation costs.

label: Morelia, Michoacán — CJNG Expansion Zone / Plan Michoacán
sub: State capital of Michoacán, a key theater of CJNG territorial expansion. On March 31, 2026, Sheinbaum announced 'Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice' — a 57-billion-peso, 12-point strategy — after street protests in Morelia and Uruapan demanding security improvements. Michoacán remains one of six states with rising homicide counts.

label: Uruapan, Michoacán — Security Protests
sub: Michoacán's second-largest city and a major avocado-producing hub with persistent CJNG presence. Street protests here and in Morelia demanding security improvements in March 2026 directly triggered Sheinbaum's announcement of Plan Michoacán on March 31, 2026. Also the city where Morena senators chanted support for Raúl Morón during Mayor Grecia Quiroz's Senate visit — an incident Sheinbaum was pressed to condemn as political gender violence.

label: AIFA Airport (Santa Lucía) — Semana Santa Record & AI Photo Controversy
sub: Felipe Ángeles International Airport recorded 164,525 passengers in 1,233 flights during Semana Santa 2026. Sheinbaum shared crowd photos on social media prompting AI-manipulation allegations she dismissed as 'hatred.' The Buenavista–AIFA train link remains delayed past the FIFA World Cup 2026 deadline due to missing safety certification.

label: Mexico–Toluca Highway — Transportistas Megablockade
sub: One of the first highways blocked in ANTAC's April 6, 2026 indefinite national megablockade spanning 20 states. Transporters and farmers demand security against highway extortion and elimination of the IEPS diesel surcharge. The Interior Ministry confirmed 3.4 billion pesos in support already disbursed but protests continued. Blockade temporarily paused April 7 after a 'responsible agreement' with state officials.

label: El Rosario, Sinaloa — Santa Fe Mine Rescue
sub: On April 8, 2026, the Mexican Army rescued Francisco Zapata Nájera after 14 days trapped in the Santa Fe mine. Sheinbaum praised SEDENA's rescue operation as an example of the military's expanded civic role under her administration.

label: Chamber of Deputies — Electoral Reform Plan B (Apr 9, 2026)
sub: On April 9, 2026, the Chamber of Deputies approved the 'Plan B' electoral reform, completing passage through both chambers. The fallback reform focuses on austerity measures for political institutions. Must be enacted by April 30 to apply to 2027 midterm elections.

label: Huamantla, Tlaxcala — First Podecobi Economic Hub
sub: Site of the first Economic Development Hub for Well-Being (Polo de Desarrollo para el Bienestar, Podecobi) inaugurated April 16, 2026. US$540M investment, 53 hectares, 6,000+ jobs in Phase 1. Focus on automotive parts, electronics, and agro-industrial processing. First of 15 planned hubs nationwide under Plan México industrial decentralization strategy.

label: Abkatun-A Platform, Campeche — Pemex Gulf Oil Spill
sub: Site of Pemex's April 2026 offshore oil spill confirmed on April 17: a leaky underwater pipeline previously covered up by operational staff. 48 beaches soiled, 915 tons of waste collected. Three employees fired. Second major Pemex environmental incident in 30 days following the March 24 Dos Bocas refinery explosion. FGR criminal negligence investigation opened. On April 20, Sheinbaum announced a presidential decree for a permanent Gulf of Mexico Observatory for hydrocarbon monitoring.

label: Buenavista Station — Tren Felipe Ángeles AIFA Link (INAUGURATED Apr 26)
sub: Mexico City terminus of the federally nationalized Suburban Train corridor. Nationalized April 23, 2026 for 5,999M pesos (CAF+Omnitren buyout). INAUGURATED April 26, 2026 by Sheinbaum and Estado de México Gov. Delfina Gómez. Full journey Buenavista–AIFA: 43 minutes, MXN $45 fare. Seven new stations, departures every 10 minutes (05:00–00:30). Serves 82,000 residents of Nextlalpan, Tultitlán, Tultepec, Jaltocan. Key FIFA World Cup 2026 infrastructure link.

label: Chihuahua City — Unauthorized CIA Drug Operation
sub: Site of the April 20, 2026 crash that killed two CIA agents (Richard Leiter Johnston III; John Dudley Black) and two Mexican AEI investigators, returning from an unauthorized joint drug-lab demolition. April 26: Security Cabinet confirmed both CIA agents lacked operational authorization. April 27: Sheinbaum blamed Chihuahua state officials directly at mañanera; LA Times reported 3 additional CIA operations in Chihuahua in 2026 without federal notification. April 28: State AG Jáuregui Moreno resigned; Gov. Maru Campos refused Senate summons. April 29: Federal probe expands, examining National Security Law violations by state officials.

label: Estadio Alfredo Harp Helú — MLB Mexico City Series 2026
sub: Home of the Diablos Rojos del México (Liga Mexicana de Béisbol); site of the 2026 MLB Mexico City Series (Arizona Diamondbacks vs San Diego Padres, April 25–26). Sheinbaum hosted both teams at the National Palace on April 24 as part of Mexico's sports tourism strategy ahead of FIFA World Cup 2026. Third MLB regular-season series in Mexico City after 2023 (Giants vs Padres) and 2024 (Astros vs Rockies).

label: Culiacán — Sinaloa Governor DOJ Indictment
sub: On April 29, 2026, the U.S. DOJ indicted Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya, Culiacán Mayor Juan de Dios Gámez Mendívil, Senator Enrique Inzunza Cazárez, former Finance Secretary Enrique Díaz Vega, and six others on charges of conspiring with Los Chapitos to import narcotics and shield cartel members — the first time a sitting Mexican governor has been charged by a foreign government. Sheinbaum April 30: 'If there are no clear proofs, the objective of these accusations is political.' May 1: Sheinbaum invoked sovereignty — 'There is a principle called sovereignty, and that isn't negotiated.' May 2: Rocha Moya requested 30-day leave via video message; state congress approved and installed Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde as interim governor; Culiacán Mayor also stepped down. FGR found insufficient evidence for extradition detention. May 4: Sheinbaum dispatched García Harfuch and Defense Secretary Trevilla Trejo to Sinaloa to coordinate with the interim government.

label: Puebla — Cinco de Mayo Sovereignty Address
sub: Site of Sheinbaum's May 5, 2026 Cinco de Mayo address, where she swore in 31,000 soldiers into National Military Service and issued her sharpest anti-interventionism statement: 'No foreign power is going to tell Mexicans how to govern ourselves.' The choice of Puebla — where Mexico defeated French forces in 1862 — was deliberately symbolic amid the CIA-Chihuahua scandal and DOJ indictment of Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya.

label: Punta Chueca, Sonora — Seri Aqueduct Inauguration
sub: On May 8, 2026, President Sheinbaum inaugurated the Seri Aqueduct at Punta Chueca — a water infrastructure project serving the indigenous Seri (Comcáac) People — as the first event of her three-day Sonora working tour. The inauguration is part of the administration's Indigenous Peoples' Justice Plans, a series of targeted investment packages for historically marginalized communities. Subsequent days include the Yaqui People's Justice Plan, land restitution decrees, and water infrastructure inaugurations in Navojoa and Ciudad Obregón.

label: Teotihuacán — Mass Shooting & Security Overhaul
sub: April 20, 2026: gunman Julio César Jasso Ramírez (27, Columbine-inspired profile) opened fire from the Pyramid of the Moon, killing one 32-year-old Canadian tourist, injuring 13 others. Jasso Ramírez died by suicide. April 22: site reopened at 8 AM with National Guard surge; Pyramid of the Moon remains closed. García Harfuch announced nationwide archaeological security review and 100,000 security forces deployed across FIFA World Cup venues. Canada issued updated travel advisory.

label: Hermosillo — Hospital General Zona 15 Inauguration
sub: On May 9, 2026, President Sheinbaum inaugurated Hospital General de Zona No. 15 'Dr. Ernesto Ramos Bours' in Hermosillo — the first event of Day 2 of her three-day Sonora working tour. The new hospital adds major public health capacity to Sonora's state capital and was part of the administration's infrastructure delivery agenda for the northwest region.

label: San Ignacio Río Muerto — Yaqui Land Restitution Decree
sub: On May 9, 2026, President Sheinbaum signed the Land Restitution Decree for the Yaqui People at San Ignacio Río Muerto, Sonora, as part of the Yaqui People's Justice Plan (Plan de Justicia del Pueblo Yaqui). She also inaugurated a school dining hall at Miguel Jaime Buitimea Elementary School. The plan restores ancestral Yaqui lands and secures water and legal rights for the indigenous Yaqui people of the Yaqui River valley — a historic debt first formalized under AMLO and carried forward by Sheinbaum.

label: Navojoa — Canal de las Pilas (Navojoa Main Canal)
sub: On May 9, 2026, President Sheinbaum delivered the first stage of the Navojoa Main Canal (Canal de las Pilas) and provided agricultural water concession titles to producers in Navojoa, Sonora. The canal addresses critical water infrastructure needs in this key wheat and vegetable production zone of southern Sonora, as part of the Sonora working tour's focus on food security and agricultural development.

label: Culiacán Las Quintas — Attack on Rocha Moya Former Residence
sub: On May 11, 2026, multiple gunshots were fired at the former personal residence of suspended Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya in Culiacán's Las Quintas neighborhood at approximately 10:12 AM local time. No injuries were reported. Sheinbaum disclosed the incident at her morning mañanera and stated that Rocha Moya — on 30-day leave following his April 29 U.S. DOJ indictment for alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties — is in Sinaloa and responsible for providing information on the attack. The incident underscores ongoing security volatility in the state during the cartel civil war.

label: Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero — Displacement Crisis + Peace Dialogue Table
sub: May 12, 2026: García Harfuch named Los Ardillos and Los Tlacos as driving a mass displacement emergency — 800+ families from Tula, Xicotlan, Acahuehuetlan, Alcozacan forced from their homes by drone and firearms attacks. May 13: Sheinbaum confirmed ~100 indigenous persons previously held by Los Ardillos were safe. May 23: Federal government formally installed the Mesa de Diálogo por la Paz for the Chilapa-Hueycantenango corridor, coordinated between Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez, Guerrero Gov. Evelyn Salgado, and community representatives; ten new municipal commissioners installed as liaisons. Guerrero remains one of six states with rising homicide counts despite the national downward trend.

label: Ciudad Obregón — Pensión Mujeres Bienestar + Mother's Day (May 10)
sub: On May 10, 2026 (Mother's Day), President Sheinbaum concluded her three-day Sonora working tour in Ciudad Obregón (Cajeme municipality) with a Pensión Mujeres Bienestar delivery event — a social program providing bimonthly 3,100-peso transfers to women aged 60–64 — accompanied by a Mother's Day concert. Sheinbaum departed for Mexico City at approx. 4:00 PM to visit her mother, Dr. Annie Pardo Cemo. Cajeme mayor Javier Lamarque Cano attended.

label: Tampico — SEMAR Artificial Reef (Onjuku)
sub: On May 13, 2026, SEMAR Admiral Raymundo Pedro Morales sank the vessel 'Onjuku' off the coast of Tampico, Tamaulipas to create an artificial reef — a marine environmental initiative attended by Tamaulipas Governor Américo Villarreal Anaya and SEMARNAT Secretary Alicia Bárcena. Officials confirmed no environmental risk from the controlled sinking. The event was part of Sheinbaum's ongoing program of infrastructure and environmental investments across Mexico's coastal states.

label: Pemex HQ — Director Change (May 14, 2026)
sub: On May 14, 2026, Sheinbaum announced Víctor Rodríguez Padilla's resignation as Pemex Director General and appointment of Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso (former CFO) as successor — the 15th cabinet change under the Sheinbaum administration. Rodríguez Padilla reduced Pemex's financial debt by ~$23B USD (down to ~$75B) and secured the company's first credit rating upgrade in over a decade. Carpio Fragoso takes the helm as USMCA talks begin and EU-Mexico trade deal approaches signing.

label: Mexico City Metro Area — Conagua 11.97B Peso Flood Prevention
sub: On May 14, 2026, the National Water Commission (Conagua) announced investments of approximately 11,972 million pesos for flood prevention infrastructure in the Mexico City Metropolitan Area and other regions, covering river desilting, expanded drainage systems, and new water treatment plants in Jalisco. Announced at Sheinbaum's Day 590 mañanera.

label: Puerto Progreso — Tren Maya Cargo Groundbreaking (May 16, 2026)
sub: On May 16, 2026, President Sheinbaum broke ground on the Multimodal Cargo Terminal of Progreso — the freight extension of the Tren Maya rail network — at Puerto Progreso, Yucatán. Two-stage construction over ~2.5 years; cargo service targeted for early 2027; 26,200 direct jobs projected. Sheinbaum also inaugurated the Hospital General Naval at Yucalpetén during the same visit, and oversaw the next phase of the deep-water port expansion in advance of the FIFA World Cup 2026.

label: Mérida — Hospital O'Horán IMSS Bienestar (24th State, May 17)
sub: On May 17, 2026, President Sheinbaum inaugurated the Hospital General 'Dr. Agustín O'Horán' of IMSS Bienestar in Mérida, Yucatán — described as the largest and most modern hospital in Latin America. The inauguration made Yucatán the 24th Mexican state to fully integrate into IMSS Bienestar; starting May 18, all health services in Yucatán are free. A total of 183 medical units and 8 hospitals were transferred to the federalized system.

label: Mexico City — U.S. DHS Mullin Bilateral Security Meeting (May 21)
sub: On May 21, 2026, U.S. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin (confirmed March 2026, replacing Kristi Noem) arrived in Mexico City for his first official bilateral security meeting with Mexico's Security Cabinet led by SSPC Secretary García Harfuch. The visit was part of the broader diplomatic de-escalation following the Sheinbaum-Trump phone call of May 16 and preceded the formal USMCA bilateral round (week of May 25). Drug czar Sara Carter's accompanying visit was postponed to May 25. Sheinbaum reiterated at her mañanera that cooperation must respect Mexico's sovereignty.

label: INE — Anti-Narco Electoral Reform Initiative (May 21)
sub: On May 21, 2026, Sheinbaum sent to Congress an initiative to create an INE Commission for Verification of Integrity of Candidacies — a new body that would consult intelligence and security agencies to screen 2027 midterm candidates for organized crime ties. Motivated by a wave of mayoral arrests under Operation Enjambre and the April 29 DOJ indictment of Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya. Framed as a tool to combat 'narco-candidacies'; opposition (PAN) warned it could be weaponized against rivals.

label: National Palace — 8th EU-Mexico Summit (May 22, 2026)
sub: On May 22, 2026, President Sheinbaum hosted the 8th EU-Mexico Summit at the National Palace — the first EU-Mexico leader-level summit in 11 years. EU Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen signed two landmark agreements: the Modernised Global Agreement (replacing the 2000 framework) and the Interim Trade Agreement (ITA, immediate effect). The ITA eliminates 95% of high Mexican tariffs on EU agricultural products, protects 568 European Geographical Indications, introduces an Investment Court System, and bans export restrictions on critical minerals. Projected 35-40% increase in bilateral trade. All 27 EU member states unanimously endorsed the deal on May 11. Strategic significance: reduces Mexico's structural dependence on the U.S. ahead of the first formal USMCA bilateral round (week of May 25), 2026.

label: Teapa, Tabasco — Day 600 Welfare Rally
sub: On May 24, 2026 (Day 600), President Sheinbaum held a large welfare rally in Teapa, Tabasco, presenting the 'Segundo Piso del Bienestar' social package — 24 billion pesos for 708,000 Tabasco beneficiaries. Announcements included the Salud Casa por Casa home health program for elderly adults, universal health service credentials allowing care at any IMSS/ISSSTE/IMSS Bienestar facility, two new hospitals (Teapa and Macuspana), Pensión Mujeres Bienestar payments to women aged 60–64, and Infonavit debt relief for 5 million families nationwide. Sheinbaum also announced her May 31 national accountability report, simultaneously broadcast to all 32 states, marking two years since her June 2024 electoral victory.

label: Tlaltizapán, Morelos — Armed Attack During Sheinbaum's State Visit
sub: May 23, 2026: An armed attack in Tlaltizapán left six dead (two police officers, one adolescent, two women, one man) while President Sheinbaum was conducting a working visit to Morelos. Violence extended statewide, with nine total victims including three femicide investigations. The incident highlights persistent security challenges in states outside the national downward homicide trend.

label: Monumento a la Revolución — Second Government Report (May 31)
sub: Site of Sheinbaum's Second Government Accountability Report on May 31, 2026 — 'En Defensa de la Soberanía.' Tens of thousands gathered as Sheinbaum addressed from the National Palace (10 AM). Key figures presented: 49% homicide reduction, $23.6B Q1 FDI record, labor poverty -3.2pp, 54,297 detained. Central message: 'Mexico is nobody's colony, nobody's protectorate.' Venue changed from Zócalo due to FIFA World Cup Fan Fest installation ahead of June 11 opener (Mexico vs. South Africa). Clara Brugada convoked supporters from 9 AM; broadcast to all 32 states simultaneously.

label: Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB)
sub: Interior Ministry headquarters at Abraham González 48, Col. Juárez. Site of CNTE-SEGOB dialogue sessions throughout the May 25–June 2026 teachers' strike. On May 29, 2026, approximately 800 CNTE Sección 22 members marched to SEGOB; seven-hour talks failed to produce agreements on core pension and salary demands, confirming the June 1 national strike escalation.

label: Ministry of Economy — USMCA Round 1 Venue (May 28–29)
sub: Headquarters of Mexico's Secretaría de Economía, led by Marcelo Ebrard. Site of USMCA Round 1 bilateral negotiations (May 28–29, 2026) between Mexico and the U.S. (Deputy USTR Jeff Goettman). Agenda: rules of origin, Chinese nearshoring restrictions, economic security framework. Round 2 in Washington June 16–17; Round 3 in Mexico City week of July 20. July 1 USMCA Joint Review deadline approaching.

label: Ángel de la Independencia — CNTE Megamarch Start (June 1)
sub: Starting point of the CNTE national strike megamarch on June 1, 2026 (Day 608). Tens of thousands of teachers from 29 states marched down Paseo de la Reforma through Centro Histórico toward the Zócalo. Major closures: Reforma, Av. Juárez, Eje Central, 5 de Mayo, Av. Madero, 16 de Septiembre. Zócalo access partially blocked by FIFA World Cup 2026 Fan Fest infrastructure. Core demands: abrogation of the 2007 ISSSTE pension reform, 100% salary increase, end of teacher evaluation system. CNTE threatened escalation if demands unmet before the June 11 World Cup opener.

label: SEP Headquarters — CNTE Stormed (June 3)
sub: Ministry of Public Education (Secretaría de Educación Pública) headquarters, Av. República de Argentina 28, Historic Center. On June 3, 2026 (Day 3 of the CNTE national strike), striking teachers stormed and occupied the entrance to SEP, forcing staff to exit. Simultaneously, teachers blocked Paseo de la Reforma for ~4 hours. Economic losses from the CNTE encampment and blockades exceeded 405 million pesos between May 25 and June 3.

label: Minatitlán, Veracruz — 93B Peso Petrochemical Investment Plan
sub: Site of President Sheinbaum's June 5, 2026 (Day 612) mañanera, held to launch the 2026–2030 Petrochemical and Fertilizer Strategic Investment Plan — committing 93 billion pesos in public and mixed investment. Expands the Minatitlán and Cosoleacaque petrochemical complexes and Pajaritos fertilizer plant. Aligns with the Pemex-Petrobras collaboration agreement for deepwater exploration announced June 2.

label: Xalapa, Veracruz — Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro Assembly (June 6)
sub: On June 6, 2026 (Day 613), President Sheinbaum led a national assembly of the Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro youth labor-training program at the Kaná Museum in Xalapa, accompanied by Veracruz Governor Rocío Nahle. Program achievements reported: 3.5 million beneficiaries, 170 billion pesos invested since 2019. Each participant receives a monthly stipend, IMSS coverage, and one year of formal work experience.

label: Tampico — ISSSTE General Hospital Inauguration (Aug 15)
sub: On August 15, 2026, President Sheinbaum and Tamaulipas Governor Américo Villarreal inaugurated the new Hospital General del ISSSTE in Tampico — a 2.3-billion-peso project reaching 250 beds and 35 medical specialties, serving roughly 564,457 ISSSTE beneficiaries. Second stop of Sheinbaum's weekend Tamaulipas work tour.

label: Ciudad Madero — IMSS-Bienestar Hospital Inauguration (Aug 16)
sub: On August 16, 2026, President Sheinbaum closed her Tamaulipas tour inaugurating the Hospital General del IMSS-Bienestar 'Heriberto Espinosa Rosales' in Ciudad Madero — a $1B+ peso investment with 179 beds and 20 specialties serving ~538,000 residents without social security, the 32nd hospital her administration has opened nationwide.

label: Mahahual, Quintana Roo — Ecotourism Protection Decree
sub: On June 5, 2026 (World Environment Day), President Sheinbaum announced a decree limiting development in Mahahual to community-based ecotourism only, prohibiting large-scale mass-tourism megaprojects. Coordinated by SEMARNAT, Sectur, Fonatur, and the Quintana Roo state government. The coastal town had faced pressure from resort developers; the decree aligns with Sheinbaum's commitment to sustainable development and SEMARNAT Secretary Alicia Bárcena's environmental agenda.

label: Zapotlán, Hidalgo — PODECOBI Industrial Pole (147B Pesos)
sub: On August 19, 2026, President Sheinbaum and Hidalgo Governor Julio Menchaca unveiled the PODECOBI industrial pole in Zapotlán: 130 projects worth 147 billion pesos across 910 hectares, projected to create 191,000 jobs. Lead investors: DEWA Capital (10.1B pesos) and Cooperativa Cruz Azul (6.5B pesos, also expanding hospital infrastructure in nearby Tula).

label: Tanhuato, Michoacán — Federal Operation Against CJNG's "Tío Lako" Cell
sub: On August 19-20, 2026, SEDENA, the National Guard, SSPC and the Navy raided a CJNG cell led by regional plaza boss Heraclio Guerrero Martínez ("Tío Lako") in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, detaining 12 people (including his daughter and partner) while he evaded capture. The operation triggered 20+ narco-blockades across Michoacán and a clash that left a preliminary 5 civilians dead.

label: Culiacán — Rocha Moya's Return, Second Leave, and Congressional Approval
sub: On August 21, 2026, suspended Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya unilaterally reincorporated himself into office, defying the April 29 U.S. DOJ indictment linking him to the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Chapitos" faction. President Sheinbaum and Morena publicly distanced themselves; Rocha requested an indefinite leave again on August 22 (6:40 p.m.), and the Sinaloa Congress unanimously approved it in an August 23 extraordinary session. Interim governor Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde, who first held the post May–August, resumed running the state pending a formal appointment.

label: Mexico City — Archivo General Agrario Inauguration
sub: On August 22, 2026, President Sheinbaum inaugurated the Centro Nacional de Atención Agraria and Archivo General Agrario, housing the Registro Agrario Nacional, the Procuraduría Agraria, and over 45,000 linear meters of historical land-tenure documents dating to 1917, plus decrees for 60,000+ hectares of Fourth Transformation land restitutions.

label: Agua Prieta, Sonora — US Cattle Export Border Reopens
sub: On August 24, 2026, the U.S. reopened the Agua Prieta (Sonora)–Douglas (Arizona) crossing to Mexican cattle exports, ending a 14-month ban imposed after New World screwworm was detected in Chiapas in November 2024. Roughly 750 head crossed on the first day under a joint SADER–SENASICA–USDA sanitary plan, with additional Chihuahua crossings to follow in a staggered rollout; the ban had blocked ~1.7 million head worth an estimated $2.2 billion.
